name: Sleep Unplugged with Dr. Chris Winter
role: Host and producer (neurologist, sleep specialist, author of The Sleep Solution)
why: A sleep neurologist's show that takes a skeptical, plain spoken look at consumer sleep trackers. That listener base is exactly the overnight tracking crowd, and he judges devices honestly rather than reviewing products.
why_now: Episode #206 'Sleep Trackers in the Clinic: Help or Harm?' aired 2026-06-01 and covered orthosomnia, sleep stage accuracy and whether data changes behaviour without guidance. That lines up with Vybe's own baseline framing.
warm_path: Cold, via the site contact form. Reference episode #206 by number.
ask: Offer to be a source, or send a short outline, on why comparing each night to your own baseline may ease tracker anxiety more than nightly scores do
opener: Hi Dr. Winter, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. I listened to episode 206 on whether sleep trackers help or harm, and your point that data rarely changes behaviour on its own stuck with me. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night only to the wearer's own baseline, with no nightly grade. If it's useful, I'm happy to be a source or send a short outline on that approach for a future episode. Do you think comparing someone to their own normal makes orthosomnia better or worse?
